blocks.text: Why you need to fix inconsistent audio levels

Audio leveling is the practice of balancing volume between different speakers or segments. When your audio levels jump around, listeners get frustrated. They have to reach for their volume dial every few minutes. This leads to listening fatigue and causes people to stop listening to your show entirely. Professional podcasts maintain a consistent volume so the listener can focus on the content rather than the technical quality.

items: Inconsistent microphone technique where guests move away from the mic.
Variations in recording environments between remote guests.
Laughter or sudden shouting that peaks above normal speech levels.
Lack of proper gain staging during the recording process.

blocks.text: How to fix inconsistent audio levels without buying new gear

You do not need expensive hardware to fix your audio. Start by setting your target loudness to -16 LUFS for stereo or -19 LUFS for mono. This is the industry standard. Use a limiter to set a true peak ceiling at -1 dBTP to prevent clipping. Focus on broad level adjustments first. Use volume automation in your DAW before you reach for a compressor. Compression should be used to smooth out the sound, not to fix massive volume gaps.

Editing audio is a deep-focus task. You cannot afford to lose your flow to administrative interruptions. When you need to check your show notes or coordinate a guest, hold your shortcut and ask Lazur to help. Lazur keeps your focus on the audio while it handles the logistics.

faq.question: What is the best loudness standard for podcasts?
faq.answer: Aim for -16 LUFS for stereo podcasts and -19 LUFS for mono podcasts to ensure compatibility across all major platforms.

faq.question: Should I use a limiter?
faq.answer: Yes, use a limiter to set a true peak ceiling at -1 dBTP. This prevents your audio from distorting when it gets loud.
